status: FIRST_GATE: ALL COSET-SHIFT (UNIVERSAL-COMPLEMENT) FACTORIZATIONS EXCLUDED; ORIGINAL_TARGET_NOT_PROVED

definitions.data: A coprime CRT split Z_n = prod_{i=1..r} Z_{m_i} (r>=1; r=1 is the trivial split) and divisors d_i of m_i with d_i>=2. kappa_i is reduction of the i-th component mod d_i.
definitions.product_factor: P = prod_i P_i, with each P_i a complete residue system mod d_i inside Z_{m_i}.
definitions.universal_complement: Q is a UNIVERSAL complement for the data if Q+P'=Z_n is direct for EVERY product factor P' with the same data.
definitions.fully_differing_pair: q,q' with kappa_i(q) != kappa_i(q') for every i.

R9_theorem.statement: WRITTEN. A universal complement contains no fully differing pair.
R9_theorem.proof: Suppose q,q' in Q are fully differing. For each i, delta_i = q_i - q'_i lies in a nonzero class mod d_i. Choose P'_i to be a complete residue system mod d_i containing 0 and delta_i, using one representative per class (0 for class 0, delta_i for its class). Then 0 and delta = q - q' both lie in P' = prod P'_i, and q = q+0 = q'+delta are two different Q+P' representations. So Q+P' is not direct, contradicting universality.
R9_theorem.coverage: Every translate of the lattice H = prod d_i Z_{m_i} is universal. A coset-shift move preserves universality: if X = c+K_I lies in Q, with K_I = prod_{i in I} d_i Z_{m_i}, then X+P' = c + (prod_{i in I} Z_{m_i} x prod_{j not in I} P'_j) for EVERY P', and this set is invariant under adding any g in prod_{i in I} Z_{m_i}. So every set reachable by FINITELY MANY coset-shift moves of ANY arity, nested or not, is universal. This includes the single-level class SZ of checkpoint-03: Szabo 1985 as described by Lagarias-Szabo 2001, whose Z_900 example was checked by hand, and Dai 2026 Definition1.1 Szabo pairs.

R8_theorem.statement: WRITTEN, plus named-import size facts. In every FACT solution (A,B), if one factor is a product factor for some data, then the other factor is NOT a universal complement for that data.
R8_theorem.orientation_alpha: Take A as the product factor. B contains 0 and 1. A component with d_i=1 would force m_i | 3,5,8,11, so m_i=1; hence every d_i>=2 and kappa_i(1-0)=1 != 0 for all i. So (0,1) is a fully differing pair in B, and R9 applies.
R8_theorem.orientation_beta: Take B as the product factor, with data e_i. By R1 and the product structure, Div(B) = {(g_i) : g_i in D_i or g_i = m_i}, excluding the all-m_i vector. The difference 3 in A forces a component with 3 | m_i and 3 not in D_i. If that m_i were odd, the B0 difference 6 would give gcd 3 in D_i; so the 2- and 3-parts share component 1. The sizes |B| divisible by 330 and |A| even (checkpoint-01 (A)) force 6 | e_1 and m_1/e_1 even. The B0 containment condition 'e_1 | delta implies m_1 | delta' for delta in {6,12} then rules out e_1 in {6,12}. So e_1 does not divide 3, and no other e_j does (they are prime to 3). Hence (0,3) is a fully differing pair in A, and R9 applies.
R8_theorem.corollary: FACT has no solution of 'product factor plus universal complement' form, in either orientation, for any coprime CRT split. This contains R6, and also excludes NESTED coset-shift constructions and Hajos-lattice (H-translate) complements of product factors.

R7_strengthened_conditional.statement: CONDITIONAL, NOT a substitute for the assigned quantifier. Hypothesis (H*): every factorization of a finite cyclic group with 0 in both factors and neither factor in a proper subgroup has, after an automorphism and factor translations, one product factor and one universal complement for some coprime CRT data. Then R2 plus R8 give not-FACT, so Shor's code C has no finite UD factor-complete superset, via the written PR interface (v2 section 2) or RSS89.
R7_strengthened_conditional.hypothesis_status: OPEN. Dai 2026 Thm1.1 proves that every such factorization of Z_{(pqr)^2} with |A|=|B|=pqr is a Szabo pair, and every Szabo pair has (H*) form. That case is irrelevant to FACT, which needs 330 | |B|. For general n, Dai writes that no essentially different example is known. (H*) is my formalization of that remark, not Dai's stated conjecture.
R7_strengthened_conditional.positive_route_reading: Any finite completion of Shor's code would yield a Sands-conjecture counterexample OUTSIDE the product-plus-universal-complement form, i.e. of a type not among the known constructions.

first_unproved_original_step: Decide FACT. Negative route: prove not-FACT, or prove (H*) at least for every n in 1320Z (open). Positive route: a FACT witness whose factors are both outside product-plus-universal-complement form. The v2 joint-delay and all-arity bridge obligations remain after FACT.

Alternatively look for a direct not-FACT mechanism using R5 plus R1. Consider consolidating R1-R9 into one route note if it remains a route control rather than an existence change.
